problem: VLN research targets indoor/terrestrial robots with static goals and near-instantaneous actions. These assumptions fail for unmanned surface vehicles (USVs), which have inertia, drift and finite turning radius, and must follow long instructions through sparse, visually repetitive river landmarks. No benchmark exists for long-horizon USV VLN in continuous rivers.
motivation: River tasks (pass a specific bridge opening, follow landmarks in order, stop near a target) need temporal evidence to tell whether a landmark is being approached or already passed. Wrong semantic transitions cannot be corrected instantly because of vessel dynamics. Semantic progress estimation and continuous motion prediction therefore have to be handled jointly.
key_idea: Decompose the instruction once into ordered, visually verifiable semantic phases, track the active phase online with a deterministic evidence-based state machine, and fuse phase, phase-specific grounding and visual-motion history in a Transformer that predicts six local SE(2) waypoints executed in a receding-horizon loop.
insight: Low single-step (teacher-forced) error does not prevent recursive drift. GNM/ViNT-style baselines have low Teacher ADE (0.0696/0.0476) but Recursive ADE of 6.24/9.89 m, versus 2.82 m for PGT-NAV. The offline ablation shows phase and temporal history are critical (Rec. ADE about 13-14 m without them), and grounding matters too (6.77 m without it). In closed loop, removing phase gives 0.00 SR and removing grounding gives 0.15 SR, so explicit progress state and phase-target association drive reliability.
method: RiverVLN benchmark: Unity-ROS river routes with bridges, signs, light gates and shoreline landmarks. 260 routes, 1,040 instructions, 108,336 samples, 6,134 phase instances and 103,472 grounding boxes. Samples are recorded every ~1 m of travel, with SE(2) pose supervision and phase-aligned annotations.

Phase decomposition: Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct is called once per episode to split the instruction into an ordered plan over 7 phases (search, approach, maneuver, pass, stop, stop-before-target, stop-near-target).

Online phase manager: a deterministic state machine advances phases from evidence (target visibility, box area, image position, motion, traveled distance, heading change). It requires 5 of the latest 8 positive observations, a minimum phase age of 15 and ordering guards, with no repeated LLM calls.

Phase-grounded temporal Transformer: tokens for the latest 20 visual frames (frozen MobileNetV3-Small), motion, language, phase and phase-specific grounding boxes go through a 3-layer, 256-d, 4-head Transformer. The head outputs 6 body-frame SE(2) increments (~1 m each).

Loss: Smooth-L1 on increments, accumulated waypoints and the execution anchor W3, circular heading loss, plus straightness, relation and stop terms. Total: L_Δ+0.5L_W+2L_exec+L_straight+0.25L_relation+L_stop.

Receding-horizon execution: predict 6 m, execute ~3 m toward anchor W3 through a map-based safety planner (A*/DWA-style) and low-level controller, then re-observe, update phase and grounding, and replan.

setting.backbone: Frozen MobileNetV3-Small visual encoder + 3-layer Transformer (trained from scratch); Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct (frozen) for one-time phase decomposition; detector-based grounding
setting.model_size: small (3-layer Transformer, 256-d); Qwen2.5-7B used only for decomposition
setting.training_data: RiverVLN Train split: 201 routes, 88,388 samples, 804 instructions (Unity-ROS simulated)
setting.observation: forward monocular RGB (1280x720 resized to 512x288) with 20-frame history plus pose/motion history; detections for grounding
setting.action_space: 6 predicted local SE(2) waypoint increments; W3 (~3 m) executed via a map-based safety planner and controller
setting.privileged: known map used by the safety planner; object detections for grounding; GT phase labels used only for training and metrics

results: PGT-NAV reaches average closed-loop SR 0.79 and SCR 0.920 in Unity-ROS, and 0.80 SR on unseen bridge-opening trials. On left/right bridge tasks it gets 0.875 SR with 0.10 collisions, versus 0.25/0.70 for GNM-style and 0.10/0.90 for ViNT-style. Offline, Recursive ADE is 2.82 m versus 6.24 m for GNM-style. Two qualitative real-USV trials succeeded.
limitations: Long multi-stage routes remain hard (SR 0.60), with accumulated phase and motion errors

Small evaluation (20 trials per category), a hand-designed state machine with detector-based grounding and a known map for the safety planner; baselines are only 'style' adaptations, not the original models
